reviews.review:
This is going to come off harsh, please remember it's just my personal experience and I have framed it as such, I have also seen others share similar sentiments so while we may be a minority we do exist.

After seeing a lot of footage, trailers, and recommendation I thought this would play a lot better than it does. For a game that takes much gameplay and mechanic inspiration from the Gears franchise it leaves a lot to be desired. It is obvious that many people either never played Gears of War 3 or haven't in a long time (which makes sense since it's ~13 years old) because the gameplay in Space Marine 2 feels like an unrefined replica of that albeit without the cover mechanic. That said for those who didn't play much of the original Gears trilogy this will probably feel like an amazing new genre (as has been depicted so much across social media).

Dislikes:
- Default FOV is narrow and uncustomisable (feels like maybe 60° to 70° by default).
- Control scheme layout feels poorly thought out, combined with the lack of sufficient customisation (certain keybinds are used by default for multiple actions but if rebound you must use seperate keys).
- The game encourages the use cover by having a short time to kill, yet explicitly wont implement a cover system because Space Marines are supposed to be tanky (this feels particularly obtuse in PvP where melee feels jank and corner peeping from range generally dominates).
- PvP multiplayer code currently has some very poor lag compensation (low latency seems to be massively advantageous from my experience).
- No player collision (I understand this could be used for griefing but it feels very cheap and breaks immersion for me especially considering Gears had it).
- Compared to Gears 3 it doesn't feel as punchy or weighty in terms of guns, animations, melee, and executions.
- Kind of a sub-point to above but stopping power and stagger don't feel well implemented specifically the lack thereof in PvP, if you melee someone you'd think it would stagger them nope, currently if you're being meleed in PvP you're better off shooting them between parrying their strikes.
- lack of weapon diversity, it feels like there should be more weapons, 80% of the arsenal feels like a bolter variation (yet there's no storm bolter) and for melee there's only 5 weapons (it just feels like melee was largely neglected in some respects).

Likes:
- the parry system is great, unfortunately it only works in specific instances and is half-baked in PvP.
- Gun-strikes are cool, once again not implemented in PvP.
- Executions are nice but feel like they could've been expanded on (Gears had different finishers for instance).
- The campaign was fun, being immersed in the 40K lore.

On the fence:
- The class system for multiplayer? feels drastically different from the campaign and completely removes interesting aspects of map design like weapon placement.
- sub-point of above the bulwark classes shield feels awesome but because the game neglects melee you end up playing very differently to how you'd imagine it would? (knight with sword and shield).
- The jump-packs feel awesome (not in coop multiplayer though).

I may revise this later if my experience changes but currently it's just frustrating and feels like a lot of wasted potential.

A short review.

I quite enjoy the game. The campaign is short, but the real longevity of the game lays in the multiplayer PVE part. Fun to play with friends. 

The graphics are just fine. Nothing special though, even if their new swarm engine works well enough.

Character costumisation is a bit lacking. Could use more heads and voice, etc. But that might come later.

Servers are bad right now, but i've still been able to play some times at least.

My main two issues with the game is blocking, it just doesn't work around 80% of the time. And yes, I do understand perfectly well how the system works and when you are supposed to press the block. There is something fundamentally wrong with the blocking though, and that needs fixing. 

Second thing is that it needs a FOV slider, or a camera distance regulator. The camera is just too damn close to the character.

Still, im having a blast! No overtly offensive current day politics in there either.

Update: Parrying/Blocking has been fixed on across the board, minus the Bulwark. Supposedly it has something to do with playing with a mouse/keyboard.

I mean.... gnuuuuh! I don't really know how to feel about this game. On the one hand, I loved Space Marine, and I'm a huge WH40k fan, and on the other, I somehow feel massively let down by this game that I was really hyped to play.

But why?

I'm going to ignore the 4 days of early access that I lost to the games inabilty to actually work on my (admitedly average) machine. I should have known better, right?

So ignoring all the weird lag in single player, that shouldn't have ever existed, I stared the single player campaign of the sequel to one of my favourite games of the last twenty years and found myself... 

Bored.

Incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bored.

50% of the single player campaign is just running through empty bits of scenery between set piece battles, pressing and holding a key to pick up ammo or grenades (why do i have to hold? just let me press a button to do a thing!!!) or even worse, to a access a lift or door you must press and hold and then wait for the  animation to complete the same three button sequence on a lift that only goes up or down... The other 50% of the game is the shooty, hack and slash gameplay veterans of SM would expect. And yet somehow, it feels lackluster.

In the first game, much of the Single Player campaign had you facing off against Orks, a familiar trope for most sci fi/fantasy fans, but especially so for 40k fans. Orks are big, dumb, funny, yet brutal warriors who are more than a match for an Adeptus Astartes. The first game did an excellent job of portraying you as Captain Titus, as an absolute bad ass who could face hordes of these green skin ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and survive. When you died, you felt like you did so cos you fought like a dumb oaf who couldn't outsmart a big dumb green chap with an axe or two.

In this latest outing, I regularly felt like I died because the game engine decided I must die, or because somehow the Emperors finest (who have been upgrade due to some weird canonical marketing ploy that I, a lifelong 40k fan, still don't fully understand), have got taller, faster, stronger, smarter, slower, weaker and dumber all at the same time.

Titus in SM2, for those who care about such things, has been through the ringer since the first game, and the story of how and why starts off as interesting and intriguing and then just deteriorates into banter between your squad mates when they ride the lift that you had to press and hold e to use ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The character of Leandros from the first game (who we all hated), is absent (or is he) only to be replaced by a carbon copy of his exact personality with a slightly more emo edge (he gets all suicidal because you get him a jump pack), and your other squad mate is also there and does something and oh ♥♥♥♥ me it's all so forgettable.

I don't know how they did it. I genuinely don't know how they managed to make this so average, it looks great, it sounds great, it has a great pedigree and the developers seem to really care about what they were making here but somehow, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, beyond all sense and reason, they made the blandest bland thing to ever emerge from blandestown.

The cynic in me, and the 40k fan, says that's because ultramarines are the focus for the story. The realist says its something else.

And it's not, like some people will excitedly scream, because of DEI, or inclusion, or "woke" or "anti woke" nonsense. It's because whoever made this game, whoever it is at the core of what this game was trying to do, failed to understand the concept of what WH40k's Adeptus Astartes represent.

Power.

Regardless of your political ideologies, your leanings, your beliefs, 40k is, like a lot this sort of stuff, about a power fantasy.

Yes, humanity is surrounded on all sides by powers that will destroy (or eat) it. Yes it's all absolutely hopeless. But here's the propaganda poster boys! The Ultramarines! And they are going to fight to the absolute death, the destruction of a system, and they might die here, but they will take some of this xenos filth with them.

Only, it doesn't feel like that for much of the single player campaign. There are moments when the ubiquitous bolter, the iconic weapon of the 41st millenium, feels like a spud gun. You empty whole clips into swarms of weak little alien beasties, who according to the lore, explode and shower the surrounding countryside in gore, and then you empty another 5, 6, 7 or 15 explosive rocket propelled grenades into their flanks, at which point they may die, or they may just surround you and repeatedly stun lock you to oblivion with a bizarre system of melee combat that wants to be Soulslike (but not too much), and fails, somehow to either be, or not be, the thing it's trying to emulate.

These problems, couple with bullet sponge enemies and floppy, floating melee combat, are only further exasperated by co-op mode, (which should be a blast, on paper) where the already weak combat is dragged down by boring level design (over it's grand total of 6 co op maps), which feature endlessly repetitive spawns, dull, uninspired mechanics, and the occasional enemy that spawns in pairs with invulnerability that requires you to empty your gun of every single bullet into it's face, and then some, before you can even consider causing them harm. Making "Operations" mode a chore to grind through, all in the name of getting a pistol that does slightly more damage under a full moon, or a new shoe that has a different colour inner sole.

The rewards for multiplayer are as uninspiring as the time my grandmother gave me a tin of salmon for my birthday. And while there are character "perks" you unlock by leveling, some of them felt so uninteresting that I'd lost interest after six hours of gameplay and genuinely started marvelling at the leveling system of the original sonic the hedgehog. 

That was satire, for those unable to spot it when it bludgeons you in the head with it's oversized, power armoured fist, as many fans of the genre seem unable to spot such things.

I played a few games of the pvp multiplayer capture the team domination nonsense, but at this point I'd lost the will to live, and was just unenthusiatically running towards the enemy wishing for a vaguely painless death, perhaps to then be surprised it had occured only in the game, and not in reality, where I could end this meaningless existence in which I occasionally have hope for some future event, like a game I have waited for for 13 years.

Still, it's not all bad. The graphics are pretty, Titus and his mates are well voiced (although I prefer the OG Titus voice actor simply because I think he carried the gravitas an Astartes should have better), and the music and environments are all what you expect from 40k IP these days. But SM2 is a clunky, odd beast, made all the more unwieldy by a slightly odd combat system that, for me, lent itself to neither mouse and keyboard controls, nor a good old XBOX controller.

I want to like it, I really do, but I can't. If I was a dramatic soul I'd say it broke my heart, but my heart was broken last year by Starfield, and by the recent upsurge in 40k fanboys with the media literacy of a dead goose.

reviews.review:
I have words on this.

There was a time Video games knew how to make a hype ending. Space Marine 1's dropped the ball, but 2's makes up for it in many ways. For anybody whose ever read a Codex or played the tabletop or took interest on the art that their friends have on their walls that depict Warhammer 40,000 and thought "Holy man on golden throne, that looks incredible/last stand as hell/awesome" this is one of those games that definitely captures the feel.

There are points in the Campaign where it does fall a little flat. The combat is nowhere near as visceral as Darktide, but then it doesn't try to be. A Space Marine can be as agile as a gymnast while wearing as much armour as a house, but that doesn't fully translate here. I am okay with this.

The actual melee combat in the game can feel janky as hell, but again I am okay with this. Bashing the enemies of man in with Chainswords, Power Swords and Thunder Hammers can be a hell of a hoot. Parrying then executing with a well placed bolt pistol strike is cathartic. It's free real estate and the game knows it.

There are Operations you can take part in with your friends and they are neatly woven into the Campaign events. Similar mission structure, but cool as hell.

My biggest issue with the game is it is unoptimised still. Plenty of desyncs with friends, the game rarely ever quits normally (I often have to task manager to close the game) and the netcode for joining lobbies often goes wrong where you can't connect to friends and have to reboot the game and hope for the best. Considering the game's themes involving the Machine Spirit, it makes some sense.

If in doubt wait for a sale or some patches to drop. I've enjoyed it so far. If Sabre are not locking fancy weapons behind paywalls, good on them. Cosmetics are fine.

Enjoying this game a ton! I had quite high expectations going into this game because I've been playing Warhammer 40K for years, and it fully lived up to them. Combat is quite thrilling; you truly feel the might of being a Space Marine every time you unleash a bolter round or chop through a horde with your chain sword. They did a fantastic job of capturing the impression of being a one-man army that can destroy anything in its way.

Also, the story, whilst short, is really captivating. It has that old-school Warhammer feel to it, dark and dramatic with plenty of epic moments that give you a sense of being a part of something very big. The graphics are very striking. The opponents' movements and reactions only serve to heighten the mayhem in these intricately drawn and evocative locations. It looks just what I envisaged a game set in the 40K universe.

Sounds and Vibe is really good too, Everything matches wonderfully to make the conflicts feel even more dramatic, including the thunder of the weaponry, the sound of the armour clanking, and the horrifying cries of the enemy. Not to mention the multiplayer, which is insanely entertaining. Engaging in combat with other players is quite exciting.

Co-op Operations mode is extremely fun, I do think they need more missions on there to stop it from going stale but the roadmap has highlighted more will be added. The PvP does feel a bit stitched on at the last minute but it is fun too, I do hope though they do add the heretic armour aesthetics onto operations mode too so that we can more unique space marines.

In my opinion, Space Marine 2 is a must-play game for everyone who like action games or is a devoted fan of Warhammer.

3rd person combat with timed button pushing isn't normally my thing, but I'm forgiving that to be a big, bad, heavily armored and genetically engineered 9' tall killing machine. The game is beautiful, runs smoothly, and has an epic backdrop that makes you feel like there's really a war going on while you do your part.

The gameplay itself is smooth and crisp, even at high settings I, with my mid tier pc, have been pushing out a steady 60-100 frames. The only issue I have is the same as the first game, the guns seem a little underpowered vs lore standards but it is still a game so I understand the liberties they've made. 

Overall, there are a few bugs and my game crashed an exponential amount of times during the last 40ish minutes of the game's campaign. But, besides that, great game. 9.5/10

[u]TL;DR:[/u] They don't make games like this anymore, and I mean that as a high compliment. You get extreme bang for your buck with 3 full modes of the game and a huge amount of free unlocks and cosmetics. On top of an extremely fun and visually stunning single player campaign that does not bore for its 10ish hour run-time.

[u]The Long Version:[/u] I miss when every game release was like this, you get a full single player campaign that took me about 11 hours to complete and that you can play entirely in co-op with up to 2 friends! You get a full left 4 dead style set of mini-campaigns for co-op with cosmetic and skill tree based customisation for classes unique to the mode. Finally, you also get a full PvP mode too! Sure this mode is clearly underbaked and not well balanced, but it's still fun! and it's not trying to be anything else, they just knew that we would all want to pit space marines against space marines to they tossed it in for free! The core gameplay loop is simple, but satisfying and fun, the story is pretty messy, but some of the character moments are great, and the visuals are truly stunning! The art direction is just fantastic, this is the first 40k game I've played to truly capture the grand, epic scale that makes it so appealing, while darktide captured the aesthetic and tone perfecctly, it stuck to smaller scale environments with a more limited scope. Space Marine 2 blows it out of the water, giving you battlefields stretching to the horizon, literal HUNDREDS of enemies at once really selling the super human power fantasy of cleaving through hordes of weaker enemies at once and the insane scale of the world, with buildings and ships covering the entire sky and all of this with enough engine optimisation that I was able to run the entire game on a mid range system at a steady 60fps with all settings on high! The lowest frame dip I ever saw was only 50fps, which is really incredible when you take into account how good this game looks. The only "microtransaction" is a season's pass that is just cosmetics, and which they have said the profits will go back into the development of the free content they are adding later on! I would love to go back to releasing games like this, it launches with a full suite of content, you pay once up front and get everything you want, and it incentives you to keep playing by having a long list of unlocks that you can ONLY unlock by just playing the game, rather than a never ending stream of limited time paid content that tries to tap into your FOMO to get you to keep playing and spending more money. On top of that it is the best representation of the 40k universe in a game yet! Even with some of it's minor flaws like repetitive gameplay by the end of the story mode or a forgettable plot, it does so much right and shows you so much you've never seen before in a game that it cannot get anything but a full recommendation from me!
A beautiful and excellent warhammer 40k game - smooth combat, excellent animations and solid PvP and truly excellent PvE multiplayer

Spoiler free review: 
A very fun game that is very worth it if you like co-op. 
The game is designed around co-op from the campaign to the PvE, you CAN, play without friends and you get bots but I've not heard that's as fun of an experience. I am saying this NOW, so the rest of the review has context. 

You can play this game in the campaign and PvE modes all in co-op, 100% of it except the tutorial at the beginning which you CAN skip but you should not since the game has mechanics that are good to know before going in. 
The campaign is pretty fun and a good romp through, played it with my brother and swapped between buddies through it. The story is a bit cliche and easy to predict what's going to happen but the presentation is wildly impressive. I do think Space Marine 1 had the better campaign over all though, but that might be because the Orks are more fun than Tyranids but that changes in both games with [THINGS THAT HAPPEN IN THE STORY] but I still enjoyed 1 more than 2 in the story aspect and even characters. But 2 is damn pretty and damn impressive.

The PvE is technically more campaign mode as you are playing the story from the perspectives and missions of other characters, except you can fully customize their looks (via unlockables) and some, of their gear. Speaking of unlockables, this is maybe a bit of a disappointment for some, these are set characters as I said, you can only bring what weapons the characters would use. So as a Vanguard, I cannot change my special skill, you are limited to either the knife or the chainsword and a bolter or melta rifle for a primary and pistol is just the bolt pistol. 
"Well that's fine, just change to another character if you don't like it" 
WEEEEEELL, the game has leveling. So you can level your character via a tree and you level your weapons. Which is very different from the campaign and it's fine- but you are going to have to grind up each, character you have interest in. 

Leveling also makes quite the difference, one of my skills I got lets me give all allies a percentage boost to melee. Which is neat. But what I'm getting to is I'm not super sure how to feel on leveling in games like this since it's fine when you're playing with friends but when someone new comes in? They always feel like the oddman out and bad no matter what you do. Either they feel bad because you lowered the difficulty so they won't get curbstomped since they have no perks or they feel bad because they do bad if you don't lower the difficulty. 

Also leveling requires you do certain things to gain parts to upgrade your character. So if you didn't fight a boss in a level? You might not get a weapon part- why is this noteworthy? The maps are always the same but the enemies that show up, aren't. So leveling can be a bit of a faff. 

One other thing to note is, this game is 3player max in campaign and PvE. So, for me personally the above and the player limit? Makes the game a bit less appealing long term. I'm not trying to say anything objective here it's just my feelings on how the game works.

I'm at the point where I prefer more simple leveling mechanics because games like Vermintide and ESPECIALLY Darktide have grind to get weapons and stats for weapons that are tedious. This is more of that and maybe I'm feeling burnout between DT and this.

CONCLUDING THIS LONG REVIEW:
Yes, I recommend this game. I don't think it's perfect, the campaign is predictable and cliche but is amazing with it's presentation.
The combat is alright with solid enough mechanics to get you through- it ain't DMC with complexity of moves but it's fun and has tons of B L O O D and a variety of weapons that if you want to explore will make for some fun. 

The leveling for me in the PvE is a bit of a downer because of how fickle the leveling seems to be but it doesn't make it bad just less appealing in the world of: I have little time and I don't want to spend it grinding in oddly specific ways. 

Fun game, love the co-op options, great presentation but also like all things it's not perfect. 
Good/10

Epic game with lots of cosmetics. Awesome campaign, great graphics, smooth animations and controls. PVE content reminding of vermintide, helldivers, darktide, etc.. Basically different classes to choose from, each with unlockable perks and tons of cosmetics, progression is also extremely steady, after every mission or nearly after every mission you will have a new cosmetic unlock. Also there may be only 6 different pve missions, but they are lengthy, hordes and enemy spawns (including bosses) are completely randomised, theres loot to find akin to vermintide which increases your rewards, and 4 difficulties to go through as your weapons and character level up.
On top of all this, theres info about the update schedule, which includes at least 3 more classes, more weapons, tons of cosmetics, new enemies and more maps..... So yeah, i can recommend it.

I love this game. The first space marine game was a huge part of my childhood, and I used to build and paint 40k models as a kid as well. That being said I was waiting for this sequel for a long long time, and it is everything I wanted it to be. Great story, multiplayer available in story mode, multiplayer operations is fun, and pvp is also fun. 

All of this is great and it’s definitely worth a buy if you are a 40k fan, or even if this is your first introduction to the 40k universe. However, I do have to mention the few negative things about the game. My main concerns are with multiplayer. There are some server issues that the devs have said they are working on that are a bit annoying, and more content for operations in particular will be needed for this game to continue to be played by a lot of people over time. Thankfully, lots of content is said to be coming including more operations and 2 additional enemy factions, as well as a horde mode. Specifics are yet to be revealed so we will have to wait and see what happens. Finally my main and really only complaint with the game is class conflict. For whatever reason duplicate classes are not allowed in PvE operations due to “balance” reasons. This is frustrating because it makes it harder to find people to play with online due to the fact that people tend to back out when they can’t play the class they want. It also makes it hard to level one specific class consistently, and personally I’m the type of person that likes to max one class before moving on to another. I feel like duplicate classes in PvE missions should be allowed, and it seems a little silly that it isn’t. Hopefully, the devs can listen to the community on the issue and lift the restrictions or add a system that automatically pairs you with people who aren’t picking the same class as you at least. All in all though this game is great and I’m excited to see what’s coming next for it. Definitely worth a buy. 10/10

9.5/10. The only thing that I wish it had would be a slightly longer campaign. It's a very good one and very good graphics and reminds me of Gears of War from the Xbox 360 days. The various difficulties are not just slightly harder from each other, it pretty much doubles in difficulty. When you go from Minimal to Average, it doubles, this from average to substantial, it doubles again. From Substantial to Ruthless, it actually triples. Not complaining, in fact I like it because it makes you work for the win every step of the way. I would say the $60 is worth it. Don't worry about getting the deluxe edition. It's just cosmetics. You don't get any "pay to win" stuff. Just different things to customize how your armor looks.
